Iran International, 23 Nov 2026

In an interview with Fox News on Sunday, Trump accused Iranian officials of stalling in talks and said they had become more aggressive than before the US midterm elections. He called Iran's negotiators "professional tap dancers" who talked constantly but said nothing of substance.

Indirect talks with Tehran were continuing, he said, but he expected the exchanges of fire between US and Iranian forces to go on.

Asked about Iranian state media reports that Iran might test the blockade, Trump said: "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy."

He also urged Iranians protesting in recent days to keep going, after seeing videos of the protests, Fox News correspondent Trey Yingst reported.

The Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday night that they had struck two radars for US Patriot air defense systems at bases in Riffa and Awali in Bahrain with missiles and drones. They called Iran's airspace a "red line" and warned of a response to any violation.

Bahrain's Interior Ministry said a civilian industrial facility had been hit and set on fire. Its Foreign Ministry rejected the Guards' account, saying the target was entirely civilian. Two people were injured, it said on Sunday: a Bahraini citizen with disabilities, whose condition was stable, and a Pakistani resident, who was in critical condition.

A US official told CBS News that the latest Iranian attacks had caused no damage to US forces or equipment in the region. It was the fourth attempted attack in Bahrain in about a week, the official said, after a pause of nearly two months.

Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Jordan and the Arab League condemned the attacks, and the Gulf Cooperation Council said it stood with Bahrain. Saudi Arabia warned that Iran would bear the consequences if they continued.

Iran's navy said on Sunday that two tankers had caught fire after hitting mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, after entering the area with their identification and navigation systems switched off. The Guards' navy separately reported explosions that had disabled two supertankers north of Ghanam Island, east of the strait, and warned shipping companies to follow its instructions.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said it had received a report of an incident between a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman and was investigating. It did not confirm the mine accounts, and it is unclear whether the reports describe one incident or several. Seven tankers have been hit in the strait since November 16, the Joint Maritime Information Centre said.

Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Sunday that talks with the United States were continuing and "the window of diplomacy is still open," but that Iran was ready for any scenario. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the state of "neither war nor peace" could not go on, and that removing the threat to Iran required "lasting deterrence."

Britain and several Arab states in the Persian Gulf have privately urged Washington not to launch new strikes, fearing Iranian retaliation and a long disruption to energy supplies, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with British government assessments.
